runs.failure_point: Judged the qualifying matter from its tax receivable agreement without opening its closing tax memorandum, and counted other groups' deals as Tax matters.

first_error.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
first_error.critic_note: The review at [80] asked for an explicit decision on the tax receivable agreement, not for the matter's other documents; no review named the closing tax memorandum.
first_error.why: The closing tax memorandum of the matter with a tax receivable agreement appeared in the agent's scan outputs and hit summaries at [25]-[49], but it read only the agreement itself and never opened the memo.

other_errors.why: The answer lists the matter whose closing tax memorandum the agent never opened as an exclusion, judging it from its tax receivable agreement, classed as benefit sharing only.

other_errors.critic_note: (specific flag) The review at [19] suggested a step to identify the practice group from metadata and the review at [80] asked to confirm each matter is in the Tax group; the agent did neither.
other_errors.why: The answer counts twelve deals from several practice groups as Tax matters on their executed tax indemnities (evidence seen at [52]-[102]).

divergence: All three runs fail the same three criteria in the same way: each excludes the one Tax matter whose qualifying evidence sits in a closing tax memorandum (listed in every run but never opened; judged from a draft markup or its tax receivable agreement), and each answers with nine to twelve M&A and other deals whose executed agreements carry tax indemnities, reading the request's Tax matters as any matter with tax indemnity work. The first error is the read-selection stage in each run. Reviews named the practice-group question in all three (T2's even suggested an agent-defined stage for it, not taken) and in T1 named the file-name filter that skipped the matter; the agents moved on. The other qualifying matter (a standalone tax indemnity agreement) was found and cited in all runs.
